memory_update.text: POWL should remain a priority underfollowed candidate for the AI data-center grid-interconnection node because company disclosures directly tie data-center orders, medium-voltage switchgear, behind-the-meter power systems, backlog, and capacity expansion.

MYRG is a plausible second-order electrical-construction beneficiary, but it needs backlog-level proof that data centers, substations, and T&D upgrades are becoming a larger mix driver rather than generic infrastructure demand.

PLPC is a speculative shadow candidate for grid hardware and substation connectors; keep it in Layer 1 only if later filings show utility capex, transmission, or data-center-adjacent grid demand flowing into orders.

For this node, the investable bottleneck appears to split into at least four public-market layers: reference electrical-equipment leaders, niche switchgear/packaged-power suppliers, electrical infrastructure contractors, and small component suppliers for T&D/substations.

Need a follow-up search focused specifically on US-listed transformer, bushing, transformer-oil, grain-oriented electrical steel, relay/protection, and cable suppliers; this pass found stronger public evidence for switchgear and electrical construction than for pure transformer components.

summary: Layer 1B expansion for the power-infrastructure chokepoint finds one reference leader and three less-obvious US-listed suppliers/contractors tied to switchgear, engineered electrical infrastructure, transmission/substation construction, and grid-line hardware. The strongest directly evidenced underfollowed name in this pass is Powell Industries, where recent company disclosures tie backlog and orders to data-center power systems. IES Holdings and MYR Group are plausible second-order beneficiaries via data-center electrical infrastructure and grid/substation construction. Preformed Line Products is a lower-confidence component/hardware hypothesis for transmission and substation buildout rather than direct AI data-center exposure.
